q: I shot a water splash at 120 fps, how do I get smooth slow motion in my 24 fps edit?
a: 1. Put the clip in the 24 fps sequence: it plays at normal speed. 2. Set Speed / Duration (`clip.speedDuration`) to 20 % (24 ÷ 120): every recorded frame is shown once, so it's smooth without made-up frames; keep Time Interpolation on Frame Sampling (`clip.setTimeInterpolation`). 3. Ripple on so the following clips move. Slower than 20 % needs Optical Flow, which can warp fast water. Sound from a slowed clip sounds wrong: use music or a splash effect instead.

q: 60fps clip in 30fps timeline, half speed looks choppy
a: At 50 % in a 30 fps sequence each 60 fps frame shows once, so it should be smooth: check the interpolation is Frame Sampling, not Frame Blending (`clip.setTimeInterpolation`), and that the clip really is 60 fps (a variable-frame-rate phone clip can stutter). Phone clips recorded at variable rates drift; record at a constant rate.

q: Slow-mo only for the moment the ball hits, normal speed around it.
a: A stepped ramp: Add Edit at the start and end of the hit (`sequence.addEdit`), the middle piece at the slow speed (e.g. 20 % for 120 fps in 24), the outer pieces at 100 %, Ripple on. Revolution has no smooth ramp curve yet (Time Remapping keyframes aren't played); a very short dissolve between the pieces softens the steps.

q: Camera shutter effect: the shot freezes with a white flash like someone took a photo.
a: 1. Insert Frame Hold Segment at the moment (`clip.insertFrameHoldSegment`). 2. A white Color Matte (File ▸ New) two or three frames long above the start of the hold, faded out with Opacity keyframes, or a quick Dip to White into the hold. 3. A shutter sound on an SFX track. 4. Optional: a white border (a shape layer frame in a graphic) and a slight tilt with Motion Rotation for a printed-photo look.

q: polaroid style frozen frame that slides off screen
a: Freeze the frame (Insert Frame Hold Segment), scale it down with a white border behind it (a white shape slightly larger than the picture, in a graphic or comp), then keyframe Position off screen with an ease-in. Nest the frame and border (`clip.nest`) so they move together.

q: Series of snapshot freezes during a montage, same look each time.
a: Build one (flash, border, sound) and save the flash and move as a preset (`presets.save`, keyframes anchored to the In point); apply it to each new hold. Keeping the sound on its own track lets you copy it with the visuals.

q: Make a shot look like it's through night-vision goggles.
a: On a node (or Lumetri): Saturation 0, then tint everything green with the Gain and Gamma wheels; lift contrast and add strong grain (`grade.param.grain.*`). A black circular vignette: an inverted ellipse window with Gain down to black, or a black Color Matte above with an inverted ellipse mask on Opacity. A slight soft glow on bright spots (Wonder Glow) sells the amplified light.

q: night vision with the binocular double circle
a: A black Color Matte on the top track with two overlapping ellipse masks on its Opacity (`masks.add`, Inverted, feathered) so two circles show the picture; the green, grainy grade on the shot underneath.

q: Thermal-ish or night-vision overlay with a HUD and timestamp.
a: Grade first (green monochrome, grain), then a graphic on top with text layers for the readouts and a few shape layers for the HUD lines. A ticking counter: Metadata & Timecode Burn-in (Video Effects ▸ Video) shows the running timecode; a real clock time needs keyframed text changes.

q: Fake a thermal camera look with hot areas yellow and cold areas purple.
a: The Duotone shader recipe maps brightness between two colours: copy it into the Effects folder (`effects.reloadUser`), set Shadows to purple and Highlights to yellow. Bright = hot, so expose so the warm subject is the brightest thing. For more than two colours you'd extend the recipe's WGSL with a third colour.

q: thermal look on a person only, background dark blue
a: Mask the person on a copy above the shot (a tracked mask on Opacity), give the copy the Duotone shader (purple to yellow) and the background a dark blue grade. No automatic person cut-out, so the mask is by hand.

q: How do I get an infrared or false-colour map look?
a: Options: the Duotone shader recipe (two colours by brightness), or write your own .wgsl effect with a colour ramp (`effects.reloadUser` loads it); shader effects run on the GPU only.

q: My underwater GoPro footage is all blue-green, how do I get the colours back?
a: 1. White balance first: pick something that should be neutral (sand, a white fin) with the picker, or push Temperature warmer and Tint towards magenta. 2. Red is lost with depth: raise Gain towards red/orange a little more than the balance alone does. 3. Contrast and a little Saturation; water is hazy. 4. Check skin on the vectorscope. Deep footage has almost no red left to bring back, so expect a limit.

q: Underwater clips at different depths look inconsistent.
a: Balance each clip on its own first node, then match them to the best one (a still of it, Shot Match, `color.matching.shot-match`), and copy a shared look node to all (`grade.append`). Check the scene for the odd one out.

q: dive video is noisy after I fixed the colour
a: Pushing red amplifies noise in the weak red channel: add spatial noise reduction on a node at the start, or temporal NR on the clip, before the colour push; grain at the end hides what's left.

q: Story-time video with white text on a black screen and my voice reading it.
a: Black Video (File ▸ New) on V1, a text graphic per line on V2 centred (align to frame), each held long enough to read twice; the voice-over recorded at the playhead (`audio.voiceover.start`) and cleaned with Clean Up Voice. Cut each line to the voice; a short dissolve between lines.

q: text story with a typing sound for each line
a: Text graphics on black, one per line, placed where you want them; a keyboard typing sound on an SFX track at each line's start. For letter-by-letter typing, per-character styles keyed by hand or a short Opacity fade per line are the options.

q: Long text story in vertical format for TikTok.
a: A 1080 × 1920 sequence, black background, large text in the middle third (out of the bottom fifth and right edge), short lines, each held long enough to read; captions on the voice if you read it.

q: Fast-forward through a boring part with a '>> 8x' label.
a: Cut the part out (`sequence.addEdit` at both ends), set it to 800 % with Speed / Duration (`clip.speedDuration`, Ripple on), and put a small text graphic '>> 8×' on V2 over it. Mute or replace its sound (sped-up audio chipmunks): a whoosh or the music.

q: VHS fast forward look with lines while it skips
a: Speed the section up (Speed / Duration), add the VHS shader effect only on that piece (scanlines, wobble), and a '▶▶' text graphic. VHS Damage at the start and end edits sells the tape jump.

q: Skip ahead in a long build video but keep it watchable.
a: Speed up the repetitive stretches (Speed / Duration 400–1600 %) with Frame Blending for smoother motion, keep the key steps at normal speed, and lay music over the fast parts. A small on-screen counter of time skipped (a text graphic) helps orientation.

q: My street scene sounds dead, how do I make it feel alive?
a: Lay an ambience bed (traffic, distant voices) on its own track under the whole scene, typed Ambience (`essentialSound.setType`); add Stereo Width for space and a few spot effects (a car passing, a door) where they appear on screen. Keep it under the dialogue (Ducking on the ambience clip if needed).

q: rain sound for a scene that should feel like it's raining
a: A rain ambience clip on its own track typed Ambience, under the whole scene with short crossfades at its ends; a darker, cooler grade helps it match. Visual rain would need overlay footage (no particles).

q: Room tone and ambience so cuts between takes don't jump.
a: A continuous ambience bed across the cuts plus room tone under dialogue gaps, both typed Ambience, with a few frames of crossfade at every audio edit.

q: Make a modern photo look like an old faded print for my documentary.
a: On the still: lower saturation, lift the blacks (master curve's bottom point up), warm the highlights or tint sepia with the Gain wheel, add grain, and a soft vignette (inverted ellipse window, Gain down). A slow push (Scale keyframes) keeps it alive on screen.

q: sepia tone on a still
a: Saturation to 0 on one node, then on the next push Gain and Gamma slightly towards orange-brown; or Lumetri with Saturation 0 and Temperature warm. Grain on top.

q: Old photo with scratches and dust overlay.
a: Grade the age (faded blacks, warm, grain), then a scratches / dust overlay clip above it with Multiply (dark marks) or Screen (light dust) blend mode. The scratches come from overlay footage, so pick one with the texture you want.

q: An end screen for my YouTube video with space for the video suggestions.
a: The last 20 seconds: a background (a blurred shot or a colour matte) and a graphic leaving clear boxes where YouTube's end-screen elements go; your logo and a short call to action as text. Save it as a template (`graphics.template.export`) so every episode uses the same layout. Music can keep running under it.

q: end card with the last shot shrinking into a corner
a: Keyframe the last clip's Motion Scale down and Position into a corner over a second (eased), with the end-card graphic underneath on V1. Leave the shrunken shot clear of YouTube's element boxes.

q: Same end screen on every video but with the episode title changing.
a: A template with only the title editable (`graphics.template.export`), applied at the end of each episode (`graphics.template.apply`); or a source graphic for the parts that never change (`graphics.upgradeToSourceGraphic`).
